sentences.text: Inawentu was a titanosaurian sauropod dinosaur belonging to the class Saurischia and the parent group Eutitanosauria.
It possessed a square-shaped jaw with a wide, squared-off snout deflected strongly downward, showing convergent similarities to rebbachisaurids like Nigersaurus and Lavocatisaurus.
The known fossil material includes a partial articulated skeleton with a nearly complete skull, twelve cervical vertebrae, ten dorsal vertebrae, six sacral vertebrae, and both ilia.
Highly modified centra and neural arches suggest Inawentu's neck was capable of multidirectional movement.
Inawentu is ecologically significant for its evolutionary convergence with rebbachisaurids, a group already extinct by this period.
Unlike related genera such as Saltasaurus and Neuquensaurus, Inawentu had narrower hips.
The holotype specimen MAU-Pv-LI-595 was discovered near Rincón de los Sauces in Neuquén Province, Argentina, and only one fossil occurrence of Inawentu has been recorded so far.
Filippi et al. announced Inawentu oslatus as a new genus and species in 2023 based on a preprint, and the genus was formally named by Filippi and colleagues in 2024.
Filippi et al. placed Inawentu in a previously unrecognized clade of square-jawed eutitanosaurs they named "Clade A".

Filippi et al. (2024) recovered Inawentu as the sister taxon to Antarctosaurus in a clade containing Bonitasaura, while a 2026 study placed Inawentu + Antarctosaurus as the sister to Brasilotitan within a basal lineage of Colossosauria.

Under equal weights, Inawentu was recovered within Aeolosaurini alongside Gondwanatitan, and Soto Núñez et al. (2026) regarded Inawentu as a probable aeolosaurine based on a matrix used in the description of Mesetasaurus.
Inawentu lived approximately 83 million years ago during the Santonian age, specifically between 85.7 and 83.6 million years ago, in what is now South America.
